_why: Generated from the post-batch-fix tree, 2026-08-15. THE NUMBER MAY FALL FREELY AND MAY NOT RISE without a human editing this file in the same commit as the code, where a reviewer sees it. Raising an entry is a decision to ship a failure the caller cannot distinguish from a real empty answer. Read the fix ladder in tools/audit_swallow_sites.py first: propagate a typed error, or carry the failure in the return value, or (best-effort paths only) narrow the except and log at ERROR. A per-file count can also rise for an innocent reason -- splitting one `except (OSError, ValueError)` into a silent FileNotFoundError branch plus a logged one scores as TWO sites, because the tool counts returns inside handlers and cannot see log levels. Say which it is in the commit message. REBASED 2026-08-18: prospector/control_center/ was deleted. Two of its files moved to prospector/ops/ and carry their counts under the new path (readers.py 1, runner.py 1) — the same sites, not new ones. Nothing rose.
_waivers_why: 7 on 2026-08-20, up from 6. One new waiver, prospector/log_shipper.py::IngestHandler.emit. This is the one shape the fix ladder cannot reach: `logging` DISCARDS what emit() returns, so no failure flag can be carried to a caller, and raising would take down code whose only mistake was to log a line. The site landed in #466 and was the reason main went red. The fix is not the waiver -- the drop is now COUNTED as `dropped_malformed` in the handler's `counters`, the same key `log_ingest` already uses on the receiving side, and handleError puts the traceback on stderr where supervisord captures it. A silent shipper and a working one now differ by a number an operator can read, which is the property the ratchet is actually protecting. Previously: 6 on 2026-08-19, up from 5. One new waiver, prospector/field_write.py::repair, around the deterministic `Field.prepare` pass added for issue #354. It is the same contract as the proposer directly below it: a field repair is best effort and must never lose a candidate that would otherwise PASS, so a broken helper degrades to "no deterministic pass" and says so in the trail. It is narrowed as far as the fix ladder allows — the failure IS carried in the return value, as a trail line the operator reads. A second candidate site in the same commit, `_expand_one_liner`, was removed instead of waived: it swallowed a config-load bug that reads identically to an undeclared glossary, and now propagates into this handler. Previously: 5 on 2026-08-18, when prospector/control_center/ was deleted with the Streamlit console and three of the waived sites went with it.
